issues.detail: The Vietnamese 'nghịch cùng' (against/opposed to) is an addition that does not correspond to the Greek text. The Greek 'κατ αυτου δικην' simply means 'demanding judgment against him'. The Vietnamese phrasing implies a specific moral or legal status of 'opposition' not present in the Greek.
The Vietnamese 'đã trình bày' (presented/stated) is a stylistic choice for 'αιτουμενοι' (asking/demanding), but it slightly softens the active demand of the Greek.
